cases.label: a(X) = 1
cases.note: The constant polynomial 1. Its value is 1 at every point, so the transform is all ones. This is the simplest test.

cases.label: a(X) = X
cases.note: The value of X at a point is the point. This transform is therefore the list of evaluation points: out[p] = psi^(2*brev(p)+1).

cases.label: a_i = i
cases.note: A ramp. It has no symmetry that can hide a mistake.

cases.label: a_i = 1
cases.note: Every coefficient is 1. The output looks random, but it is only this polynomial at N different points.

cases.label: a(X) = 3 + 5X^(N-1)
cases.note: Two non-zero coefficients. One is at the top degree, where X^N = -1 becomes important.

cases.label: pseudo-random coefficients
cases.note: What a real ciphertext polynomial looks like: uniform residues mod q. A fixed-seed xorshift64* generates them, so the trace repeats exactly.

cases.label: a_i = q-1
cases.note: Every coefficient is at the largest residue. The conditional subtractions inside the butterfly then run.

convolutions.label: X * X = X^2
convolutions.note: The simplest product. Nothing passes the top degree.

convolutions.label: X^(N-1) * X = X^N = -1
convolutions.note: The purpose of this ring. The product passes degree N, returns to degree 0, and changes sign.
